This is both a test article and a writing reference. Its source is a single
readable Markdown file, `index.qmd`. Edit it and save: the live preview refreshes
automatically. No HTML wrappers, CSS, or JavaScript are needed to write a post.

## Mathematical notation

Let $R\subseteq X\times X$ be a reduction relation. Write $x\to_R y$ for one
step and $x\to_R^* y$ for its reflexive, transitive closure:

$$
x_0\to_R x_1\to_R\cdots\to_R x_n.
$$

Aligned equations use ordinary LaTeX notation:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{size}(\mathrm{leaf}) &= 1, \\
\operatorname{size}(\mathrm{node}(s,t))
  &= 1+\operatorname{size}(s)+\operatorname{size}(t).
\end{aligned}
$$

Use `$...$` for inline mathematics and `$$...$$` for a displayed equation.

## Theorems and folded proofs

::: {#def-normal-form}
## Normal form

An element $n\in X$ is a **normal form** if there is no $y$ such that $n\to_R y$.
:::

::: {#def-confluence}
## Confluence

A relation $R$ is **confluent** if, whenever $x\to_R^* y$ and $x\to_R^* z$,
there is a $w$ with $y\to_R^* w$ and $z\to_R^* w$.
:::

::: {#thm-unique-normal-form}
## Uniqueness of normal forms

If $R$ is confluent, $x\to_R^* n_1$, and $x\to_R^* n_2$, where $n_1$ and $n_2$
are normal forms, then $n_1=n_2$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Proof"}

Confluence gives a common reduct $w$:

$$
n_1\to_R^* w\qquad\text{and}\qquad n_2\to_R^* w.
$$

Because $n_1$ is a normal form, its reduction to $w$ must have zero steps.
Thus $n_1=w$. Likewise, $n_2=w$, giving $n_1=n_2$.

$\square$
:::

::: {#cor-canonical}
## Canonical results

If $R$ is terminating and confluent, each element has a unique normal form.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Proof of the corollary"}

Termination ensures that reduction reaches a normal form. By
@thm-unique-normal-form, any two normal forms reached from the same element
coincide.

$\square$
:::

Quarto numbers statements and resolves references such as
`@thm-unique-normal-form` automatically. Definitions, lemmas, and corollaries
use `#def-`, `#lem-`, and `#cor-` labels respectively.

### Copyable statement and proof

````markdown
::: {#thm-your-label}
## Your theorem name

Your statement, with $x=y$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Proof"}

Write your proof in Markdown and LaTeX.

$\square$
:::

Refer to @thm-your-label.
````

Set `collapse="false"` for a proof that starts open but can still be folded.

## Inference rules

Here are the variable and application rules of the simply typed lambda calculus:

$$
\frac{x:A\in\Gamma}{\Gamma\vdash x:A}\;\text{(Var)}
\qquad
\frac{\Gamma\vdash f:A\to B\qquad\Gamma\vdash a:A}
     {\Gamma\vdash f\,a:B}\;\text{(App)}
$$

Abstraction discharges an assumption:

$$
\frac{\Gamma,x:A\vdash t:B}
     {\Gamma\vdash\lambda x.t:A\to B}\;\text{(Abs)}
$$

Fractions can be nested to build derivation trees:

$$
\frac{
  \displaystyle\frac{x:A\in\Gamma,x:A}{\Gamma,x:A\vdash x:A}\;\text{(Var)}
}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda x.x:A\to A}\;\text{(Abs)}
$$

### Copyable rule

```latex
$$
\frac{\Gamma\vdash f:A\to B\qquad\Gamma\vdash a:A}
     {\Gamma\vdash f\,a:B}\;\text{(App)}
$$
```

## Category theoretic diagrams

Let $F,G:\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}$ be functors and let $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$
be a natural transformation. For each $f:A\to B$, this square commutes:

$$
\require{amscd}
\begin{CD}
F(A) @>{\eta_A}>> G(A) \\
@V{F(f)}VV @VV{G(f)}V \\
F(B) @>>{\eta_B}> G(B)
\end{CD}
$$

In other words, $G(f)\circ\eta_A=\eta_B\circ F(f)$.

Here is a pullback square:

$$
\require{amscd}
\begin{CD}
P @>{p_2}>> B \\
@V{p_1}VV @VV{g}V \\
A @>>{f}> C
\end{CD}
$$

Its universal property says that, whenever $u:X\to A$ and $v:X\to B$ satisfy
$f\circ u=g\circ v$, there is a unique $h:X\to P$ with
$p_1\circ h=u$ and $p_2\circ h=v$.

### Copyable diagram

```latex
$$
\require{amscd}
\begin{CD}
F(A) @>{\eta_A}>> G(A) \\
@V{F(f)}VV @VV{G(f)}V \\
F(B) @>>{\eta_B}> G(B)
\end{CD}
$$
```

This notation supports rectangular diagrams. For diagonal arrows and more
elaborate diagrams, export an SVG from [quiver](https://q.uiver.app/), save it
**beside this post**, and embed it with `![Diagram description](diagram.svg)`.
Keep the quiver share link or TeX source alongside it for later editing.

```lean
  exact h
```
